newsitem.title: CHINA: Crime, corruption biggest fears in Hong Kong - poll.
newsitem.headline: Crime, corruption biggest fears in Hong Kong - poll.

text.p: Rising crime and corruption are Hong Kong people's biggest concerns now that the territory has been handed back to China, a poll conducted by the Sunday Hong Kong Standard said.

Of 300 people asked last week to chose their greatest concerns among law and order, the economy, a stable government and corruption, 82 people, or 27 percent, said their biggest concern was a breakdown in law and order, the newspaper said.
A further 81 people said they were mostly concerned about a rise in corruption following Hong Kong's July 1 return to Chinese rule.
Stable government was the most important issue for 24 percent of the people questioned, while 22 percent said the economy was the biggest concern, the newspaper said.
